clue.text: He became proverbially rich from various 5 across

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the referenced answer can be set out in differing arrangements

parts.note: the clue points to the answer of 5 across, SOURCES

explanation.surface: A tale of a man who made his fortune from many different streams of income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from various 5 across' looks like a story of diverse income; 'various' tells you to rearrange the letters of the 5-across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient king of Lydia was so wealthy that 'as rich as' him became a proverb for great riches.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill touring Middle East for fun

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the showman's name goes round the region

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William Cody, the American showman

explanation.surface: The Wild West showman takes his act on tour of the Middle East for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is humour or amusement, things done for fun.

clue.text: Point to hold forth about and elaborate

indicators.note: about means the speech-making verb goes round the compass letter

explanation.surface: A speaker making a point at length and in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' looks like a verb continuing the speech, but it is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means richly decorated or complex, which is what elaborate means as an adjective.

clue.text: Dreadful Australian orgy

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shocking Aussie party gets out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman festival became a byword for unrestrained revelry, so it can mean a wild orgy.

clue.text: Post the money for the pool's entry?

definitions.text: the money for the pool's entry?
definitions.meaning: the sum a gambler puts into a betting pool

explanation.surface: Paying to join the betting pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden pole and a gambler's wager share the same word.

clue.text: Origins of Crusoe's shipwreck

indicators.note: a wreck smashes a ship to pieces, so the letters of the name are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the name of Defoe's castaway with its S included as a letter

explanation.surface: How Robinson Crusoe's adventure began: with his ship going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' fits the castaway story perfectly but is the anagram signal; here the S of the possessive is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sources are the places or things from which something starts, so they are its origins.

clue.text: Upset over what's broadcast

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about something they heard on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset over' reads as being annoyed about, but 'Upset' scrambles OVER WHAT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: This radio band of short wavelengths is used for long-distance broadcasting.

clue.text: Put out, nothing is fit for the job

indicators.note: out suggests something disordered, so the word put is rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed that a worthless candidate is judged suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT to give UPT; add O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to a task is an idiom for being capable of doing it.

clue.text: Reason and method for walking across water

parts.note: a reason is a cause
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: Explaining why and how someone might walk on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised path over water or marsh, built so people can cross on foot.

clue.text: They guard the southern gates

parts.note: gates are entrances, entries

explanation.surface: Watchmen stationed at the south entrances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries are soldiers posted to keep watch, people who guard.

clue.text: Artist returns two hours before noon

indicators.note: returns means the time phrase is read backwards, going back the way it came

parts.note: two hours before noon is ten in the morning, written TEN AM

explanation.surface: A painter comes back to the studio at ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like the artist coming back, but it turns TEN AM round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French painter, a forerunner of Impressionism, so he is an artist.

clue.text: A call for military revolution

parts.note: reads like a summons to an armed uprising, but is the drill command telling soldiers to turn and face the opposite way

explanation.surface: A rallying cry urging the army to overthrow the government.
explanation.definitionFit: This parade-ground order makes soldiers revolve through half a circle, a literal military revolution.

clue.text: Cleaners put off by public conveniences

parts.note: to put off is to discourage, or deter
the gents is a British term for a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: Office cleaners who refuse to deal with the public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTS is everyday British for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are washing agents, substances used for cleaning.

clue.text: Will him to succeed

parts.note: reads as urging someone on to success, but describes a person named in a will to take over property or a title

explanation.surface: Willing someone on to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a will to inherit and take over from the deceased is the one who succeeds them.

clue.text: Property tax will keep the gamekeeper busy

definitions.meaning: a tax levied on a dead person's property
the work a keeper must do across a country estate

explanation.surface: An inheritance tax that keeps the estate's keeper hard at work.
explanation.walkthrough: This British death duty has since been replaced by Inheritance Tax.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a tax on property passed on at death, and a keeper's job on a landed estate is literally his duty there.

clue.text: Tax I am able to declare in Rome

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
am able means can
to declare is to state

explanation.surface: Someone declaring their tax liability while living in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'in Rome': the enclave the answer names lies within the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal enclave ruled by the Pope is located within the Italian capital.

clue.text: Formerly, patients treated outside hospital

explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges PATIENTS to INTEPAST; 'outside' puts it round H.

clue.text: Crazy to take two banned substances

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: It would be mad to take two illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or mad person, used attributively for something crazy.

clue.text: Makes a timely entrance?

parts.note: reads as arriving at just the right moment, but describes recording one's arrival at work on a time clock

explanation.surface: Arriving at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who registers arrival at the workplace on a time recorder does so with a timely entrance.

clue.text: Healthily, Ron gets involved in sexual activity

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Ron takes up a healthy approach to his love life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved in' reads as Ron joining in; 'gets involved' scrambles HEALTHILY and RON.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal idiom means a bout of lovemaking, originally a romp among the haystacks.

clue.text: Does it fly on a wing and a prayer?

definitions.text: Does it fly on a wing and a prayer?

parts.words: Does it fly on a wing and a prayer?
parts.note: the idiom for scraping through hints at an insect with wings whose raised forelegs look like hands in prayer

clue.text: Balls hit high, right into the heavens

parts.note: the heavens are the skies

explanation.surface: Cricket balls struck straight up into the sky.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot a bird

definitions.meaning: to raise the hammer of a gun ready for firing
the male domestic fowl, a rooster

clue.text: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't big enough

parts.note: a bag is the amount of game shot in a day; a poor tally could cost the keeper his job, or have him fetch a larger sack

clue.text: He's in race with a foreign character

indicators.note: in puts the pronoun inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
he, with 's as is

clue.text: Two officers, one gun

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
Lt is a lieutenant

explanation.surface: Two officers who share a single firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colt is a make of revolver, so one example of a gun.

clue.text: Music said to get in the dough

indicators.note: to get in places one word inside the other, the spoken word going into the dough

parts.note: a dough is a soft mixture like a paste
said means spoken, oral

explanation.surface: Music that is supposed to help you earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound-alike signal and tempts solvers towards pasta, but it supplies a spoken-word synonym; 'to get in' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical composition evoking shepherds and country life.

clue.text: It returns in June, having got the tip-off it's free

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the shortened month
tip-off means the tip, the first letter, is removed from the month
returns means the word it is read backwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns IT round; 'having got the tip-off' removes the first letter of the month, leaving UNE; 'in' places the turned pair inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo bonds, so to set free.

clue.text: One at kindergarten showing very little spirit

a tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum

explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests courage, but it is a drink: a tot of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny tot is an informal phrase for a very young child, such as a kindergarten pupil.

clue.text: Beasts of burden going round by deep gorges

indicators.note: going round means the animals surround the next word

parts.note: asses, donkeys, carry loads
taken as written
